examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of a Quotient Given the Necessary Data
examples.problem:
The values of functions $h(x)$ and $z(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=-1$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $h(x)$ | $z(x)$ | $h'(x)$ | $z'(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-1$ | $-4$ | $2$ | $6$ | $3$ |

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{h(x)}{z(x)}\right)$ at $x=-1.$
examples.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{h(x)}{z(x)}\right) = \dfrac{h'(x)z(x)-h(x)z'(x)}{(z(x))^2}.
$$

At the point where $x=-1$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{h(x)}{z(x)})|}_{x=-1} & =\frac{{h}^{′}(-1)z(-1)-h(-1){z}^{′}(-1)}{(z(-1))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 2-(-4)\cdot 3}{{2}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{24}{4} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
For the function $f(x)$ and $g(x)$, you're given the following data:

$$
f(2)=-1,\,{f}^{′}(2)=3,\,g(2)=2,\,{g}^{′}(2)=-3
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=2.$ 

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=2}=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x)) & =f(x){g}^{′}(x)+g(x){f}^{′}(x).\end{aligned}
$$

At the point where $x=2$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=2} & =f(2){g}^{′}(2)+g(2){f}^{′}(2) \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-3)+2\cdot 3 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
